Having worked in kitchens before, this is the best game I've found that simulates kitchen teamwork. If you've played the popular game "Overcooked" and thought "I wish the kitchens weren't so wacky, unrealistic, and unreliable, so we could actually maintain a system within the team", then this game is for you. Players can actually assume meaningful roles within the kitchen/dining room if they want, and it works well.

There's just enough change after every level to keep a session fun/refreshing. This game can get difficult, which is a plus. I play it occasionally with friends, and it seems like nearly every time we play, there's a new update that adds content.

Will be great if we can XXL map without mod. Ur banquet map isn't big enough. 

Or you can let us buy more space. I think that is a good update to the game.

If you're the kind of gamer who: 
 
- Likes the co-op chaos of Overcooked, but prefers a touch of rogue-like upgrading and progression 
- Needs multiple different avenues to run your kitchen, with dozens of options for foods, tools, furniture, and appliances 
- Also enjoys a little spice added with different locations, layouts and sometimes seasonal themed kitchens 
- Wants to turn into a crane 
 
And can deal with: 
- At times feeling like you are either nearly getting to customers before they're fed up, or you literally are so secure you barely need the fourth person 
- Games feeling like they take a little longer then they need to at times, getting to overtime days can be a multiple hour challenge 
 
Then you'll be serving cats steak in no time. 
 
A popular game night choice among the gamers, I'd recommend this to anyone looking for the classic chef-together experience made a little bit more challenging then just stand-alone mini games. Plate up has you making choices - do we want to add an extra dish that will require us to get a new ingredient and change up our strategy, or should we just not be able to see what our customers order? And you can upgrade most of the tools you find to buy at the end of every day. 
 
You will slowly evolve your kitchen into a conveyor belt sushi place. It is the most efficient evolution, the ultimate eatery. Good luck getting there.

We had a blast playing this together, and if she were still here, I know she'd definitely would have wanted to play this again with me, so from me, I thank you so incredibly much.

If you're comparing this to Overcooked when thinking of buying it, here's how I compare the two: Overcooked was a much higher stress and faster-paced game, but Plate Up! is actually more relaxing. I like that it's a roguelike type of game, and losing actually just makes the game easier. I like it far more than Overcooked, and I recommend you give it a try if Overcooked was stressful for you, but you liked the gameplay.

Oh, Plate Up is so much fun. I honestly prefer it to overcooked, which is most likely because of the fact that I just really love roguelikes. There is so much to do, and it's phenomenal. There are also less bugs compared to overcooked.

If you have at least one other person to play with, I definitely recommend getting this game. I got it on sale, but I'd say it's also worth the full price if you plan to play it a lot.

I only played it with friends, so I can't say anything about singleplayer, but I had fun. Something to note: not everyone liked it, or liked it as much as the others. I would have liked the runs to be shorter, maybe 12 days instead of 15, as they can get repetitive.

In fact, if you automate things well, you'll eventually need fewer players, and some can even leave the game without making a difference. That's not really great for a party game. [h1] Get that pizza ready! [/h1]
A fun little management cooking game that's perfect for a few “relaxing” rounds with your friends.

[h3] Gameplay [/h3]
Essentially, you play as a chef who takes customers' orders and then prepares their meals in the kitchen, following a series of different steps. So far, we've only tried four different dishes: pizza, steak, salads, and coffee. All of them were pretty easy to understand and prepare, and serving them felt genuinely satisfying.

The longer you keep your restaurant running, the more stars you earn, which unlocks additional upgrades for your restaurant. You can get a better stove, more counter space, or more plates for your waitstaff, for example.

We did about five runs in total, and with each run, we managed to last a little longer. I really enjoyed seeing how every run unlocked new recipes, items, and layouts that made the game and future runs a little easier.

[h3] What I didn't like [/h3]
We played it as a two-player game, and honestly, I thought it was going to be a cozy little cooking game. Nope. Not even close. As soon as a ONE customer doesn't get the order or has to wait too long, you lose the game. Eventually, we reached a point where it felt practically impossible for the two of us to keep up.

The doors? An absolute nightmare. We ended up having to install mods just to stop them from constantly getting in the way. And playing with keyboard controls was absolute hell. More than once, I somehow ended up putting tomatoes

[h1]Fun Gameplay, but Needs a UI Overhaul[/h1]

I really want to love this game because the concepts are fresh, but the [b]UX/UI frustration[/b] makes it hard to recommend in its current state.

Binding controller buttons is a thing so common in games that it should not be this awfully implemented.

Very frustrating is the item collection. In a game where time is your biggest enemy, having to struggle with picking up the correct thing is annoying at best. I've lost multiple runs not due to the interaction behaving poorly.

[b]Dear Devs:[/b] Please prioritize a "Quality of Life" update for item targeting and UX/UI!

[h1]Intro[/h1]
[i]PlateUp![/i] is a restaurant management roguelite where you and possibly your friends manage a restaurant until it closes. You'll take orders, cook their food, serve them, and clean their plates, doing fast enough so the next customer don't wait for too long for their turn.

[b]Pros:[/b]
- Different playstyle when played solo or coop
- Different recipes with different difficulty
- A lot of room to experiment
- Accessibility options for those who want to make the game harder or easier

[b]Cons:[/b]
- Smaller maps limit you from going further after the endgame

[b]Specs[/b]
AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 16GB RAM, AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT

[h1]Should you buy this game?[/h1]
[i]If you enjoy playing restaurant management game that focus on cooking and serving the customers, buy this game.[/i]

[i]PlateUp![/i] is a restaurant simulator roguelike where you run a restaurant. Your main goal is to make sure that it's not closed, which is achieved by serving all available customers without running out their patience. Each day has a certain number of customers that will increase on the next day. The game has 15 main days in total, which will extend into overtime days after you finish it, allowing for endless
Agency over how your kitchen is set up is the biggest draw for me in this game.  It's a lot of fun with friends and also by yourself.

PlateUp! is cozy chaos turned all the way up. On the surface it looks like a cutesy restaurant sim right? But once the orders start stacking, it turns into pure panic. You’re cooking, serving, cleaning, upgrading, and yelling at your friends all at the same time while customers slowly lose patience. It’s fast, stressful, and incredibly addictive in that “just one more day” way. 
 
What makes it shine is the rogue like progression, every run feels different depending on your layout, upgrades, and menu choices. Things can spiral out of control fast, especially in co-op, but that’s where the fun is. Solo is tense and strategic, multiplayer is absolute chaos. It’s not flashy, but it nails that "Overcooked" style energy while adding way more depth and replay value. Perfect for friendships you’re willing to risk.
